speak.title: Role-play: Grandmother's painting
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.role: the cousin who wants to keep it
a.text: You and your cousin have inherited a valuable painting from your grandmother. You want to keep it in the family home, where she hung it. Explain why it matters to you, and listen to your cousin's idea.

b.role: the cousin who wants to lend it
b.text: A local museum has asked to show the painting for a year. You think more people should see it. Explain your idea, and try to find an arrangement you can both accept.

phrases: I'd hate to see it leave the family.
That's a fair point, but more people could enjoy it.
What if we lent it for six months?
I don't think it's right to give it away.
We'd still own it, wouldn't we?
Let's try to find a compromise.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: where did the painting end up, and was it a fair decision?
